sources_read: .qc-cache/kittle-2026-10-09-r3/rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx (sheet 'Quality Checks' row 54 = #53 task_is_distinct_and_authored; sheet 'Internal Quality Checks' row 54 = #53, no internal annotation in columns E-G for this row; the row 53 annotation there belongs to #52 task_security_and_secrets)
Sibling list: projects/ (39 directories) and a grep of sibling task.toml files for messaging/chat
evidence: The task is written for its own product. instruction.md:1-3 describes a small law firm (Kittle & Rowe) whose clients email documents to whoever answered last. It names two firm-specific priorities: ethical walls (a conflicted person learns nothing from any corner of the app) and retention (disappearing-message timers, partner legal holds that survive timers, and permanent deletion). walls-and-retention.md:15-35 develops the legal concepts: Dev walled from M-12; Harriet adds and lifts walls live; matter timers of off/1/7/30 days measured against the fixed clock; holds cover exactly one message and override timers until released; transcripts serve as the firm's record of a matter. The seed (matters M-11 'Pryce lease dispute' 7d, M-12 'Marsh Holdings acquisition' off, M-13 'Pryce will' 30d) and the accounts (Partner, Associates, Clients) use legal-domain data. The 16 graded criteria in tests/scored/functional/judge.toml are dominated by those concepts: 4 wall criteria (signin_and_client_scope, wall_every_route, wall_mentions_and_links, wall_added_live), 3 retention criteria (deleted_and_expired_messages, timer_changes, hold_scope_and_release) and search_and_transcript. The remaining criteria cover ordinary chat features (nested_replies, edits_and_stale_edit, safe_formatting, message_links, unread_and_new_messages_line, sent_once_in_order, live_updates_keep_my_work, persistence), and each is tied back to the domain: walls in mentions and links, held messages in edits, transcripts in formatting. Sibling comparison: (1) threadline-chat, the only other dedicated chat task, is a Slack-style team workspace with channels, DMs, reactions, pins, presence/typing, incoming webhooks with idempotency and an append-only audit (threadline instruction.md:3-204). Kittle has none of channels, DMs, reactions, pins, presence or webhooks, and Threadline has no walls, timers, holds or transcripts. Both share generic chat primitives (threads, edits, unread, search, dedupe), which is expected for the category and not a noun swap. Threadline also uses the legacy APP_MANIFEST shape, while Kittle uses the staged template. (2) hireops-recruiting-operations includes candidate conversations with unread counts and live updates that preserve the draft. Its core, though, is a pipeline board with interview capacity, batch move/undo and concurrency refusals, which do not appear in Kittle. (3) The integration.md text shared with HireOps and Colderwater (Node 22 /app/server.js, port 3000, DB_PATH, health endpoint, no symlinks, external CDN allowed) is shared runtime policy, not cloned product content. The closing line 'Before you hand it over ... make sure nothing breaks' (instruction.md:9) echoes HireOps instruction.md:13 but lists Kittle-specific actions (open a transcript). A residue grep of the frozen task for hireops|threadline|pellmoor|colderwater|docketlight|torquebay|oriel|drawbill|recruit|channel|webhook|snippet found only legitimate uses ('search snippets' in the Kittle notes, the generic 'empty workspace' in the shared judge gate boilerplate, and a local variable named 'candidate' in server.js:23-25). Template: every CHANGE_ME in rules/projects/webdev-task-template (task.toml name, description, keywords, difficulty, category, provenance, arena_slice; instruction.md; seed; notes) is replaced with Kittle-specific content in the frozen task.toml and files. Domain plan: task.toml category 'Messaging & Chat Interfaces' and arena_slice 'full-stack-express-sqlite-messaging-chat-kittle-matter-chat' fit a legitimate suite category. The workspace has no separate written domain-plan document, so suite fit is judged from the category and sibling concepts only (see note). Adversarial check for this row: a 'nouns-swapped Threadline' (rename channels to matters, users to clients) would lack walls, timers, holds and transcripts and would fail most of the 16 criteria, so the task cannot be satisfied by a sibling clone. A conforming alternative (different layout or routes) is not penalised on distinctness grounds, because app_context.md:24-27 and functional prompt.md:36-57 accept any routes and payload shapes. This row is a source/authoring judgment; no runtime evidence is required for it.
note: Non-blocking: the suite has two chat-category tasks (threadline-chat and kittle-matter-chat), and HireOps also has a conversation sub-feature. They are differentiated by concept (team workspace vs legal ethical walls/retention vs recruiting pipeline), but no written suite domain plan exists in the workspace to confirm intended category allocation. The owner may want to confirm with the lead that a second Messaging & Chat task is planned.
